title: Periodic Bragg Stack Centered on Visible Stopband
scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave Bragg stack with 7 HfO2/SiO2 pairs centered at 550 nm will achieve high visible reflectance while maintaining adequate telecom transmittance, with performance improving monotonically as pair count increases up to the 30-layer limit.
design_principle: Bragg interference from periodic high-low index contrasts creates a photonic stopband centered at the design wavelength; quarter-wave optical thickness maximizes reflectance bandwidth for a given pair count.
proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) x 7 | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 14 layers
Center wavelength of the quarter-wave condition
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Minimize layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 14 (well under 30-layer limit)
Quarter-wave thicknesses are manufacturable with standard deposition control
HfO2/SiO2 pair is space-qualified per L03, L15, L33
theory_basis: Bragg reflector theory for 1D photonic crystals
Quarter-wave stack design for maximum stopband reflectance
known_risks: Stopband may not cover full 400-700 nm range with only 7 pairs
Telecom transmittance may suffer from residual stopband tails
Limited design freedom compared to non-periodic approaches
execution_request_english: Design a 14-layer periodic Bragg stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand) (7 pairs, high-index layer first). Optimize individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Initial thicknesses set to quarter-wave optical thickness at 550 nm center wavelength. Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Substrate: SiO2 (Lemarchand) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light.
